Answer: B
Reason: Scimitar syndrome is characterized by partial anomalous pulmonary venous return from the right lung to the IVC, creating a curvilinear "scimitar" opacity on CXR, and is typically associated with right lung hypoplasia (often involving the right upper lobe) and dextroposition of the heart. Option B correctly identifies these hallmark features (right-sided opacity, dextroposition, and RUL absence/hypoplasia), whereas the other options describe findings inconsistent with this syndrome (e.g., hyperinflation, left-sided pathology, or drainage into the SVC).
